question: Did you live in California for all of last year?
why_ask: Full-year residents file Form 540; part-year residents and nonresidents file Form 540NR.
retrieval_query: California resident part-year resident nonresident

question: Did you live or work in more than one state last year?
why_ask: Income earned in another state can create a filing requirement there and a California credit.
retrieval_query: income from another state California other state tax credit

question: Were you (or your spouse, if married) born before January 2, 1961?
why_ask: People 65 or older get a larger standard deduction and the new senior deduction on Schedule 1-A; California gives a senior exemption credit.
retrieval_query: standard deduction age 65 or older additional amount

question: Could anyone else, such as a parent, claim you as a dependent on their tax return?
why_ask: A taxpayer who can be claimed by someone else has a smaller standard deduction and cannot claim dependents.
retrieval_query: can someone claim you as a dependent standard deduction dependent

question: Were you a U.S. citizen for all of last year?
why_ask: Non-citizens may be resident or nonresident aliens for tax purposes, which changes the return.
retrieval_query: resident alien nonresident alien who must file

question: Were you a full-time student at any time during last year?
why_ask: Student status affects education credits and whether someone can claim you.
retrieval_query: full-time student definition education credits

question: Are you legally blind or totally and permanently disabled?
why_ask: Blindness increases the standard deduction; disability can affect credits and retirement income.
retrieval_query: additional standard deduction blind

question: Did you own, receive, sell or trade any digital assets, such as cryptocurrency, last year?
why_ask: Digital-asset transactions must be reported and may create gains or income.
retrieval_query: digital assets question Form 1040

question: What was your marital status on December 31 last year?
why_ask: Marital status on the last day of the year decides which filing statuses are possible.
retrieval_query: marital status filing status last day of the year

question: Did you and your spouse live apart for all of the last six months of the year?
why_ask: Married people who lived apart may qualify as head of household.
retrieval_query: considered unmarried head of household lived apart last 6 months

question: Did you get married, divorced or legally separated during last year?
why_ask: A change in marital status during the year changes the filing status options.
retrieval_query: divorced or separated filing status

question: Did anyone live with you, or did you support anyone, such as a child or a relative?
why_ask: Dependents affect filing status and several credits. A yes opens the family questions.
retrieval_query: who qualifies as a dependent qualifying child qualifying relative

question: Did you work as an employee and receive a W-2?
why_ask: Wages are reported from Form W-2.
retrieval_query: wages salaries Form W-2

question: How many jobs did you have last year?
why_ask: With two or more employers, too much Social Security tax may have been withheld.
retrieval_query: excess social security tax withheld more than one employer

question: Did you receive tips at work?
why_ask: Tips are taxable; qualified tips may also qualify for the new deduction on Schedule 1-A.
retrieval_query: tips income deduction for qualified tips Schedule 1-A

question: Were you paid overtime last year?
why_ask: Qualified overtime pay may qualify for the new deduction on Schedule 1-A.
retrieval_query: qualified overtime compensation deduction Schedule 1-A

question: Did you earn money on your own, for example contract or freelance work, driving for Uber or DoorDash, or selling things online?
why_ask: Self-employment and gig income go on Schedule C and may owe self-employment tax. A yes opens the side-business questions.
retrieval_query: self-employment income gig economy Schedule C who must file
origin: Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2025) Part III; gig wording from Form 13614-C (Rev. 10-2026)

question: Did you receive Social Security, a pension, an annuity, or money from a retirement account?
why_ask: Retirement income is reported from SSA-1099 and 1099-R. A yes opens the retirement questions.
retrieval_query: social security benefits pensions annuities taxable

question: Did you rent out a house, an apartment or a room?
why_ask: Rental income and expenses go on Schedule E. A yes opens the rental questions.
retrieval_query: rental income and expenses Schedule E

question: Did you receive unemployment benefits?
why_ask: Unemployment compensation is taxable federally; California does not tax it.
retrieval_query: unemployment compensation taxable

question: Did you receive a refund of state or local income tax last year?
why_ask: A state refund can be taxable if you itemized deductions the year before.
retrieval_query: state income tax refund taxable itemized

question: Did you receive interest or dividends, for example from a bank account or bonds?
why_ask: Interest and dividends are reported from 1099-INT and 1099-DIV.
retrieval_query: interest income dividends taxable

question: Did you sell any stocks, bonds or real estate?
why_ask: Sales must be reported with gains or losses.
retrieval_query: capital gains and losses sale of stock

question: Did you receive alimony?
why_ask: Alimony from agreements made before 2019 is taxable.
retrieval_query: alimony received taxable divorce agreement before 2019

question: Did you have any gambling or lottery winnings?
why_ask: Gambling winnings are taxable.
retrieval_query: gambling winnings taxable

question: Did you receive any other money, such as cash payments, jury duty pay, awards or royalties?
why_ask: Other income may be taxable and is outside the common cases.
retrieval_query: other income taxable jury duty awards

question: Did you pay mortgage interest on your home?
why_ask: Mortgage interest is deductible if you itemize.
retrieval_query: home mortgage interest deduction itemized

question: Did you pay real estate (property) taxes?
why_ask: State and local taxes, including property tax, are deductible if you itemize.
retrieval_query: state and local taxes deduction real estate taxes

question: Did you pay large medical, dental or prescription costs yourself?
why_ask: Medical expenses above a share of income are deductible if you itemize.
retrieval_query: medical and dental expenses deduction threshold

question: Did you give money or goods to charity?
why_ask: Charitable contributions may be deductible; keep receipts.
retrieval_query: charitable contributions deduction records

question: Did you pay interest on a student loan?
why_ask: Student loan interest may be deductible without itemizing.
retrieval_query: student loan interest deduction

question: Did you put money into a retirement account, such as an IRA or 401(k)?
why_ask: Some contributions are deductible and may qualify for the saver's credit.
retrieval_query: IRA contributions deduction saver's credit

question: Are you a K-12 teacher or aide who paid for classroom supplies yourself?
why_ask: Eligible educators can deduct some classroom expenses.
retrieval_query: educator expenses deduction

question: Did you pay alimony (not child support)?
why_ask: Alimony paid under agreements made before 2019 is deductible.
retrieval_query: alimony paid deduction

question: Did you or anyone in your family take college, technical or job-related classes?
why_ask: Tuition may qualify for an education credit.
retrieval_query: education credits American opportunity lifetime learning

question: Did you or your employer put money into a Health Savings Account (HSA), or did you take money out of one?
why_ask: HSA contributions are deductible federally but not in California, so they are added back on Schedule CA.
retrieval_query: health savings account California adjustment Schedule CA

question: Did you buy health insurance through Covered California or the Marketplace?
why_ask: Marketplace coverage requires Form 1095-A to reconcile the premium tax credit.
retrieval_query: premium tax credit Form 1095-A marketplace

question: Did you buy a new vehicle with a loan last year?
why_ask: Interest on a qualifying new-vehicle loan may be deductible on Schedule 1-A.
retrieval_query: car loan interest deduction qualified passenger vehicle Schedule 1-A

question: Did you buy and install energy-saving home items, such as windows, a furnace or insulation?
why_ask: Some home energy improvements qualified for a credit in 2025 (Form 5695).
retrieval_query: energy efficient home improvement credit Form 5695

question: Did you sell a home?
why_ask: A home sale may be partly or fully excluded from income.
retrieval_query: sale of main home exclusion

question: Was any credit card, mortgage or other debt cancelled or forgiven?
why_ask: Cancelled debt is usually taxable unless an exception applies.
retrieval_query: cancellation of debt income exceptions

question: Did you have a loss from a federally declared disaster?
why_ask: Disaster losses have special rules.
retrieval_query: casualty loss federally declared disaster

question: Did the IRS ever deny a credit you claimed, such as the earned income credit or child tax credit?
why_ask: A prior disallowance can require an extra form to claim the credit again.
retrieval_query: credit disallowed Form 8862 earned income credit

question: Did you receive any letter or bill from the IRS?
why_ask: An open IRS notice must be handled before or with the return.
retrieval_query: IRS notice letter respond

question: Did you make estimated tax payments to the IRS or the FTB, or apply last year's refund to this year?
why_ask: Estimated payments are credited against this year's tax.
retrieval_query: estimated tax payments credit
